Definition: a primary particle; "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative):--(X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with. In composition (as a prefix) it usually denotes separation, departure, cessation, completion, reversal, etc.
BiblicalUsage: The little word ‘from’ — off, away, out of — and it carries half the New Testament on its back. ‘From that time Jesus began to preach’ in Matthew 4:17, and Jesus, knowing He was come from God and went to God, in John 13:3: the same small word marks where a ministry begins and where a Saviour came from and returns to.
TheologicalSignificance: No doctrine hides in a preposition, but the whole gospel runs through this one — from God, from sin, from death, and back to God again.
